text: checker-100 measurements, 2026-11-11 (public GETs to ccel.org only; the XML parsed with python -I and ElementTree, no network). (1) Volumes: https://www.ccel.org/ccel/aquinas/catena1.xml 200, 3,021,275 bytes, sha256 943a6b5fd668ef021877e99f210d96b84abbbe81212fe5627c6bb206f9ce1618, the same bytes as the lead's copy on two fetches; catena2.xml 200, 971,399 bytes, sha256 69c8f2d198186de50e444c6a618dd3de24d3b89e8af879042b06c5a46c89168f (Mark); catena3.xml and catena4.xml 404 on www and on the bare host, as are /catena3, /catena3/catena3 and catena3.html; CCEL's Aquinas page lists the Catena Aurea for Matthew and Mark only. (2) Encoding: both declare UTF-8 and decode strictly as UTF-8; curly quotes U+201C, U+201D, U+2018, U+2019 (Matthew 4426, 4357, 573, 1890), 2,813 U+00A0 in Matthew; no C1 controls, no mojibake, the only entity is &. The broken quote marks were a console artifact: Python printing to a redirected Windows stdout writes cp1252 bytes (0x91 for a left single quote), which then read as invalid UTF-8; reproduced. catena2 carries an external DOCTYPE (ThML10.dtd) and no entity declarations. (3) Structure: a div2 per chapter with a chapter-level scripCom (osisRef Bible:Matt.1 etc.); no note elements; inside comment paragraphs only scripRef (894 Matthew, 242 Mark; 33 in Matthew have no osisRef, such as 'Ep. i.' inside the head of ii.i-p29), pb page breaks mid-sentence (842, 251), Hebrew and Greek spans (98 in Matthew) and one img (ii.i-p96, inside an editors' note). No comment paragraph comes before a chapter's first scripture paragraph. (4) Verse keys: 1,063 scripture paragraphs in Matthew and 684 in Mark; one carries an osisRef for its own verse (ii.i-p1, Matt 1:1), none in Mark. (5) Heads: 6,110 comment paragraphs in Matthew and 2,458 in Mark; 1,267 and 656 open with no author; 84 and 64 distinct heads; 131 and 66 editors' notes open mid-paragraph; about 160 margin notes in Matthew. (6) Neither file holds a list of writers: the front matter is the title page (both) and Mark's preface, which names the translator John Dobree Dalgairns, while the DC metadata names William Whiston as translator of both. (7) Rights: DC.Rights is empty in both, and each carries the comment 'Copyright Christian Classics Ethereal Library'; the work-info pages carry no rights line; ccel.org/about/copyright.html says most editions are based on books public domain in the United States, that they may hold copyrighted special contents, and asks permission to republish CCEL works or use them commercially.

findings: SOURCE, TESTS and LIVE (plan line 2): CCEL serves two of the four volumes. catena1.xml (Matthew) and catena2.xml (Mark) answer 200; catena3.xml and catena4.xml answer 404 on www and on the bare host, as do /catena3, /catena3/catena3 and catena3.html, and CCEL's Aquinas page lists the Catena Aurea for Matthew and Mark only. So there is no Luke or John at the named source. Three criteria cannot be met: 'John 1:1 ... returns Catena excerpts', the LIVE check of John 1:1, and '200 excerpts across all four Gospels'. Worse, the Matthew volume cites John 1:1 three times inside excerpts (scripRef ii.i-p26.1, in the Pseudo-Athanasius excerpt on Matt 1:1). A build keyed on scripRef osisRefs, as SOURCE says, would pass the John 1:1 test by serving Matthew 1:1's commentary. To answer: either name a source and a rights basis for Luke and John, or narrow the goal, the tests and LIVE to Matthew and Mark (for example Mark 1:1 in place of John 1:1); and add a test that no Catena block is keyed by a cross-reference.

SOURCE 'one block per verse or range as the scripRef gives it', and the goal's 'a paragraph of class scripture whose scripRef carries an osisRef ... for each verse or range': this holds for one paragraph. Of 1,063 scripture paragraphs in Matthew, only ii.i-p1 (Matt 1:1) carries its own verse's osisRef; of 684 in Mark, none does. The verse is leading text ('2.', '3-6.', '6-8.'), and some of it is mistyped: 'l.' for 1 (ii.xiv-p1, ii.xvii-p1, ii.xviii-p1, ii.xix-p1, ii.xxi-p1, ii.xxiv-p1), '3l.' (ii.xiii-p158), '21,' '32,' '33,' (ii.xii-p71, ii.xiii-p159, ii.xv-p164), '[30]' (ii.xxiv-p191), and '65' and '66' with no point (ii.xxvii-p299, p300). Ranges overlap (3-6 then 6-8 in Matt 1). The order is the Vulgate's: in Matt 5, verse 5 comes before verse 4, with an editors' note saying so. One set of comments follows a run of up to 17 scripture paragraphs (Matt 5:1-3 share one), so a block is a run, not a verse. In Mark, the only scripRefs in scripture paragraphs are cross-references (Mal 3:1 at iii.i-p9, Isa 40:3 at iii.i-p10, Isa 53:12 in ch. 15), so a scripRef-keyed build files Mark 1:2-3's comments under Malachi and Isaiah. class=scripture is also set on two Fathers' paragraphs, iii.xi-p11 'Chrys.:' and iii.xv-p57 'Theophylact:', which a class-based parse would drop as Scripture. Today's layout gives a block one int verse, and for_ref (commentary.py:168-176) skips any block whose verse is not an int. To answer: define the key as the div2 chapter plus the leading verse text of each run of scripture paragraphs; state the rule for mistyped numbers, overlapping ranges and out-of-order verses; add a range field to the layout; and test on these ids.

FIDELITY 'each excerpt keeps its own attribution as printed', and the goal's 'paragraphs each opening with its author': many paragraphs open with no author. In Matthew, 1,267 of 6,110 comment paragraphs do (continuations such as ii.i-p7, ii.i-p19, ii.i-p27); in Mark, 656 of 2,458. In Mark, about 400 paragraphs open with 'It goes on:', 'There follows:', 'Wherefore it goes on:' and the like: Aquinas's link, quoting the Gospel's next words, not an author. Sentence colons also look like heads ('Phares is interpreted:', 'He says:', 'Or:', 'Thus:'). Under 'an attribution the table does not hold reads as printed', 'It goes on' would be served as an author, and a Gospel quotation as a Father's words. About 160 margin notes such as '[margin note: Aug., Enchir. c. 38]' change the ascription mid-paragraph. To answer: state that a paragraph with no head continues the excerpt before it; that a link phrase is lemma text, never an author; how a head is told from a sentence colon (for example, a closed list of heads); and how margin notes are kept. Test on these ids.

FIDELITY: the editors' notes, and the 200-excerpt test. The editors' matter is neither one marker nor a whole paragraph. '[ed. note: ...]' opens mid-paragraph, inside the Father's words, 131 times in Matthew and 66 in Mark (ii.i-p4, Pseudo-Chrys.). Other forms: the lettered '[ed. note, a: ...]' (47), '[margin note: ...]' and '[marg. note ...]' (about 160; Mark's preface says the margin carries the editors' corrected readings), '[note: ...]' and '(note: messenger)'. One note runs across paragraphs (ii.i-p15 to ii.i-p16; p16's 'Gregory of Nazianzus' text is the editors'). Ten Matthew paragraphs have unbalanced brackets, and CCEL's own '[Isa 53:8]' scripRef brackets use the same syntax. Against this, the test as written requires each excerpt to equal 'the source XML's text for the same paragraph', with only whitespace and encoding normalized. It can pass only if the notes stay in the Father's words, which contradicts the editors'-note criterion, or if the test reuses the tool's own splitting, which is circular. An excerpt is also often several paragraphs. And the full XML is not in the gate's clean worktree: nothing under data/ is committed, there is no network fetch, and the fixture is 'small'. So the sample either skips in the gate or needs about 4 MB of CCEL XML committed. To answer: define the check independently of the parser, for example a lossless partition (head, the Father's words and the separated notes, in order, equal the source paragraphs' text); and name the command and the place where the full volumes are compared.

FIDELITY 'a table ... with the author's dates and Greek or Latin, built from the edition's own list of writers'; SOURCE_META 'translator'; TESTS 'each attributed to a named Father': neither file holds a list of writers. The front matter is the title page (both) and Mark's preface; the first volume's prefatory remarks, which Mark's preface points to, are not in CCEL's file; and the edition gives no dates and no Greek or Latin. CCEL's DC metadata names William Whiston as translator of both volumes. That is wrong: Mark's preface names John Dobree Dalgairns, and the translator differs by volume. Several heads are not Fathers, and some wrote after 1054: Theophylact (359 in Mark), the Gloss (Gloss., Gloss. ord., Gloss. interlin., Gloss. ap. Anselm; 300 or more), Remigius, Rabanus, Anselm, Lanfranc, Petrus Alfonsus, Josephus and the councils. Matthew 5:3's block holds 'Gloss. interlin.', 'Remig.' and 'Rabanus', so 'each attributed to a named Father' cannot hold there unless the Gloss is called a Father. The edition's own editors dispute some ascriptions: the note at ii.i-p15 gives the 'Hilary' passage to Hilary the Deacon, and Mark's preface says most 'Chrys.' passages are Victor of Antioch's and that the 'Jerome' commentary is spurious. Mapping 'Hilary' to Hilary of Poitiers, with his dates, is then a guess. To answer: name the public-domain source of each row's dates and language, cited per row; take the translator per volume from that volume's preface; type each entry (Father, later writer, gloss, council); serve the mapping as Aquinas's ascription; and have the tests say 'a named author in the table'.

BASE and LIVE 'the shelf is built on the box by the run's tool': no gated ship path runs a tool on the box. tools/deploy.sh snapshots, transfers, restarts, runs the on-box gates and checks drift; it never runs a build. docs/HARNESS.md:130 says 'Only the lead touches the box, and only through a gated ship path, never by hand'. Checker-5's plan verdict in 2026-11-01-green-suite (ledger line 3) recorded the same gap: 'tools/deploy.sh never runs seeds, and the lead may touch the box only through deploy.sh'. A build run after deploy.sh would also run after its gates, so nothing would grade or roll back the shelf it writes, and nothing tests the box's outbound fetch from ccel.org. To answer: name the path, for example a build script reviewed in the step with its own read-back, its refusal on a hash mismatch and its undo, run through a named gated route, and say what the LIVE check reads to show the build ran.

SOURCE 'checked under the strict PD-only gate ... with CCEL's own statement for each volume quoted': CCEL's statement for each volume is no public-domain statement. In both files DC.Rights is empty and the only notice is the comment 'Copyright Christian Classics Ethereal Library'; the work-info pages carry no rights line. ccel.org/about/copyright.html says most editions are 'based on books that are public domain in the United States' but 'may have copyrighted introductions, cover art, and other special contents', and asks you to 'Contact us for permission to republish CCEL works or to use them commercially'. The files also carry CCEL's own staff-written description and CCEL's inserted reference brackets. So the quote the criterion requires is a copyright claim, and the step's checker cannot read it as support for public domain. To answer: rest the reason on the 1841-45 date of the printed text alone; say what of CCEL's additions is not carried (the description, the inserted brackets) and how the repository fixture, which is cut from CCEL's file, stands; or name a scan of the printed edition.

SHELF 'nothing served today changes' against 'the commentary tool and the site name the sources that cover a verse', and TESTS 'each red at the base': as written, these contradict each other and cannot be observed. A list of covering sources added to the /commentary or MCP response changes the default Henry response; the MCP description '(Matthew Henry)' changes; and 'the site' names no page (site/bible.html, wisdom.html and console.html all render /commentary). 'Matthew Henry on John 3:16 reads exactly as at the base' cannot be red at the base. The verse lookup (commentary.py:168-176) falls back to blocks[0], another verse's commentary, which the Catena criterion forbids. The lookup must therefore branch by source, while Henry's test_for_ref_verse_between_blocks_uses_earlier_block still holds. To answer: state which fields of Henry's response stay byte-equal (for example the whole response for ref John 3:16, pinned from the base); where the list of sources lives (a named new key or a new route); the site page and the text a reader sees there; and take the regression test out of 'each red at the base'.

The OCR of vol. 3 reads Luke 1:3-4 'to write unto thee in order ... That thou mightest know', with 'shews' 57, 'hath' 130, 'saith' 12, and its marginal citations interleaved into the text ('Aug.de', 'Ambr.'). findings: MEASURE and THE GOLDEN (plan two, line 5): the plan does not require the chosen source's words to be the 1841-45 printing's, and its preference points at a source whose words are not. isidore.co is the only candidate holding all four Gospels as text, and it states no rights, so 'a source with no such request is preferred' picks it. But its Matthew and Mark lost every quotation mark (11,298 and 3,668 U+FFFD, no curly quotes), and its Matthew is CCEL's transcription (the same '3l.' typo, the same '[ed. note:' and reference-bracket forms), so CCEL's permission request follows it. Its Luke and John are modernized. Luke 1:3-4 there reads 'to write to you in order ... That you might know', while the 1843 printing (archive.org catenaaureacomme03thomuoft) reads 'to write unto thee in order ... That thou mightest know'. 'shews', 'hath' and 'saith' occur 0 times in isidore's Luke, against 57, 130 and 12 in the scan of that volume's Part I. A golden transcribed from that source and 'checked against the scan' would differ from the scan, and the plan gives no rule for what a difference means. So the shelf could serve a modern editor's wording as 'the English edition of 1841-45', on a public-domain reason that covers only the printing. To answer, make it checkable: the golden holds the printing's words, each excerpt equal to the scan, with any difference listed and justified as a named transcription typo; a source whose golden excerpts differ from the scan beyond such typos is not chosen; a source's permission status follows the transcription it copies, not the host serving it; and the census records, for each source, its replacement-character count and its archaic-form counts against the scan.

Step catena, whose scope cannot widen, is abandoned with the tree put back and its gated content (d4be63f7b955) saved by its builder; it reopens as step catena2, whose scope adds tests/test_box_build.py, tools/catena_aurea/golden.json and tools/catena_aurea/authors.json, and whose note proves the saved content re-applied before any change.

MEASURE changes nothing served. It surveys the 1841-45 printing's scans on archive.org (each volume and part, its item id and its rights mark quoted), the scans' own OCR text, and the transcriptions: CCEL's catena1 and catena2, and isidore.co's four pages, whose Matthew and Mark copy CCEL's transcription and whose Luke and John are modernized (checker-100, line 6). For each it records which Gospels it holds, its rights statement, its count of replacement characters, its counts of the printing's old forms (such as shews, hath, saith, thee, thou) against the scan's, and the structure census: verse marks and their variants and typos, ranges, continuation paragraphs, quoted Gospel text such as 'It goes on:', margin notes that change the attribution, and editors' notes. The words served are the printing's. A transcription that differs from the scan beyond listed transcription typos is never served; a transcription's permission follows the transcription it copies, not the site that hosts it, so CCEL's transcription and isidore.co's copy of it are compared against, never served, unless CCEL grants permission. The step names, for each volume part of each Gospel, two archive.org items that are scans of different physical copies of the 1841-45 printing, each with its own OCR, by item id and the chapters each holds (checker-100 found that catenaaureacomme03thomuoft holds Luke I-X while catenaaureacomme03thom holds I-XXIV, so Luke XI-XXIV needs a third item, probably p2catenaaureacom03thomuoft), and the share of excerpts it expects to serve; no OCR is run by this run. A chapter without two such copies is named for a later run and not served here. It also records which layout file each item offers (such as the OCR's page XML with word coordinates), since the rules below read it.

THE GOLDEN, committed at step measure: at least 30 excerpts for every Gospel this run serves, chosen by a fixed seed and including the hard cases the census found (a range, a continuation, an inline editor's note, a margin note, a quoted 'It goes on:'). Each holds the printing's words as read from the scan's page image: copied by code from one copy's OCR and checked word by word against that page image by eye, every correction listed and applied by code, normalized only by folding curly quotes and removing a space before punctuation, with the archive.org item and page, its verse or range, its author as printed, its citation, and its editors' notes kept apart. The step's checker checks each against the page image. The golden is the test of the parser and of the confirming reading; neither makes it. Among the hard cases: an excerpt that runs across a page break, an excerpt beside a margin citation, a page with a footnote, a running head inside an excerpt's span, a word with a real hyphen at a line end (such as 'money-changer'), and an author's name in small capitals. Also: an excerpt that begins mid-line, and an author's name standing inside another Father's words, which must stay his words and never start an excerpt. Step catena2 corrects two verse fields, each read again from the page image and listed as a correction applied by code: John-s20-p216 is John 6:1-14 and Luke-s11-p292 is Luke 8:40-48 (builder-30, line 49: both copies' ranges and running heads give them so).

AUTHORS: a committed table holds every attribution the census finds, each with dates read from its article in the Catholic Encyclopedia (1907-14, public domain) as the golden is read, from the page image with corrections listed, stored as printed or left out with the reason, and with Greek or Latin only where the article states it, else 'not stated'; writers after the age of the Fathers, such as the Gloss, Remigius and Rabanus, are labelled later writers; 'Pseudo-' authors stay distinct; an ascription the editors dispute is kept with their mark. An attribution the table does not hold is served as printed and never guessed. The shelf names itself the Fathers and later writers that Aquinas gathered, in the English edition of 1841-45, crediting the translators as the edition's own prefaces name them, never a catalogue's metadata. In Mark, the head CHRYS. is served as printed with the editors' mark the author table already quotes from Mark's preface, which gives most of those passages to Victor of Antioch; there it is never named John Chrysostom without that mark.

CATENA: the build fetches, for each volume part served, both copies' OCR layout files with word coordinates and the small-capitals flag, parses them streaming, never whole, and runs under its listed memory cap with the full build's peak recorded in the step's note; and from each copy, before any comparison, removes the page furniture by its place on the page as the coordinates give it: the running head and page number at the top, footnotes below the text, and the margin column, whose text is kept apart as the citations of the excerpts it stands beside and is never part of a Father's words. Line-end hyphens are read by one stated rule: a hyphen is kept where the hyphenated form occurs elsewhere in that volume's text and the joined form does not, joined where the joined form occurs and the hyphenated does not, and otherwise the excerpt is held. An excerpt starts only at an author heading: a name or abbreviation the author table holds, set in small capitals as the layout file flags it, followed by ';' or '.', after a full name or an abbreviation alike, wherever on the line it falls; both copies must show the heading at the same place, or the excerpt is held. A name not flagged as small capitals, or followed by neither ';' nor '.', is words, never a heading. Before any comparison, five holds target the errors two copies of one typesetting share: an excerpt is held where a line's last word and the next line's first word together form a word found elsewhere in that volume (a lost hyphen), where any word's box crosses the text column's edge (a margin word fused into the text), where the ligature ae or a word read as 'ae' occurs, where a token holds a character outside letters and the stated punctuation (. , ; : ? ! ' " ( ) - and the dash, with '&' only in '&c.') or is on the census's list of misreadings (such as 'fyc.' for '&c.'), and where a word is flagged as a superscript but is not a footnote mark answered by a footnote on that page (as 'that' in John 1:3), in each case unless the page image check in the golden has settled that word. An excerpt is served only when its words, as read from the two copies after these steps and the stated normalization (whitespace, declared encoding), are equal; its author is served only when both copies give the same name after folding small capitals and case, else the excerpt is held; its citation is served only when both copies' margin readings agree after the same folding, else it is served as 'citation not confirmed' and counted. Every held excerpt and unconfirmed citation is counted per Gospel in the step's note against the measure step's expectation, and every golden excerpt the build serves equals the golden, words, author and citation. A range is stored as a range, with a field this source adds and the other sources never read. A paragraph continues the excerpt above only where the printing's structure shows it; a paragraph the parser cannot attribute with certainty is not served and is counted. Editors' notes are never served as a Father's words. Parsing never touches the network beyond the named fetches and never resolves an external entity or document type definition. The tool exits non-zero on any golden mismatch or changed source, so no build directory is added. The tool imports only the standard library and is deterministic; the step adds its entry to tools/box_builds.txt with the output's sha256, a memory cap, and its inputs: the author table, the golden, the item ids and chapters per volume part, and the pinned hashes of every file it fetches, which reach the box with the tool; the tool reads no other repository file, and the listed hash comes from a run with exactly these inputs; and src/concordance/build_pins.json gains the same hash. The tool writes its output as bytes with '\n' line ends on every platform, so the hash computed on Windows is the hash the box computes. A section's verse or range is served only when both copies read it alike and it falls in order between the sections before and after it in its chapter, since both copies of one typesetting can misread a verse mark alike (Matthew-s10-p32 reads 1:2 in both, where the page prints 1:12-15); a golden excerpt whose verse both copies confirm and which differs from the golden refuses the build, as a mismatch in words, author or citation does. The italic-I hold reads the case as printed and holds an italic run whose first word is lower case where a sentence or the excerpt begins, whatever the word, since a list of verbs misses the verbs it does not name. Each golden excerpt the build matches to no head is named in the step's note with the reason.

SHELF: commentary.py reads catena-aurea only from data/builds/catena-aurea/<the pinned hash>/, a missing build reading as not built; SOURCE_META gains catena-aurea with name, author, license and via (tools/card_commentary_verses.py:85 reads author and license with no guard). For catena-aurea, a verse the Catena does not reach reads as no commentary there, never another verse's; commentary.py:176's fallback to blocks[0] stays as it is for the other sources, and that it serves another verse's words is named as a want. Matthew Henry's response for every reference is byte-identical to the base. Which sources cover a verse is answered by a separate request (GET /commentary with sources=1, and the MCP tool's matching argument), never by a change to the default response; site/bible.html, which shows commentary today, offers the Catena beside Henry where it covers the verse. The step adds live probes that read Matthew 1:1's Catena excerpts. Since the live assay refuses only a probe that has passed before (tools/live_assay.py:19-22), the first ship is graded by the --build-verify chain and the ship note above; from then on the assay guards these probes as it guards every probe. The MCP commentary tool's description names catena-aurea and the argument that lists which sources cover a verse, so a caller finds both from the tool list (builder-30, line 49).

TESTS, red at the base where they move: Matthew 1:1 returns every golden excerpt the build serves there, word for word, with Pseudo-Chrysostom kept distinct from Chrysostom, and Jerome and Rabanus, which the build holds there because their two copies read otherwise, absent and never shown under another name; the Gloss is labelled a later writer, tested at Matthew 1:17, since Matthew 5:3's Gloss is held; Mark's CHRYS. is served with the editors' mark; a section whose verse both copies misread alike is held (Matthew-s10-p32); an editor's note never appears in a Father's words; a verse the Catena does not reach reads as none for catena-aurea; a reference that names John is tested only if the chosen source holds John. Guards that hold at the base and after: Henry's response on John 3:16 and on a sampled set of references is byte-identical; the other sources read as before. The build refuses a changed source and a golden mismatch. Parsing is tested on committed fixtures cut from the chosen source, never a network fetch.

UNCHANGED: the gate's assay, the floor and the moat hold; the full suite passes against the baseline; no file under data/ is committed. LATER, named: Chrysostom's homilies and Augustine (Schaff's Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers), Haydock's Catholic commentary, the four senses of Scripture as tags with the literal first, and the Gospels the chosen source lacks. LIVE: after the deploy and its build, the requests are GET https://narrowhighway.com/commentary?ref=Matthew%201:1&source=catena-aurea, the same with sources=1, and GET https://narrowhighway.com/commentary?ref=John%203:16 for Henry; and, the only POSTs allowed, a read-only MCP tools/call of commentary with the same arguments at both MCP doors, https://narrowhighway.com/mcp (the site engine) and https://api.narrowhighway.com/mcp (the dedicated MCP host). The expected reading: every Catena excerpt served for Matthew 1:1 equals its golden entry in words, author and citation (or 'citation not confirmed' where the build's note counts it so); excerpts held are counted against the build's note; at least one excerpt is served; the sources=1 answer names catena-aurea beside Henry; and Henry's response on John 3:16 is byte-equal to its reading before the deploy at the site and at both MCP doors. The engines' restart counts are read before and after by the lead. tests/test_box_build.py's listing test checks the canary and canary-fail entries by name, so a real build may be listed beside them; what it pins of those two entries is unchanged.
goal: The commentary shelf carries the Church Fathers on the Gospels, verse by verse, in their own recorded words, each excerpt attributed as printed. The owner, 2026-11-11, on making Catholic and Orthodox Christianity a strength: 'Run down the list. This needs to be a strength.' Measured at master 85c3dda: the shelf (src/concordance/commentary.py, built by tools/migrate_commentary.py from bible.helloao.org) serves Matthew Henry, Adam Clarke and John Gill, all Protestant, and that API offers no Catholic or Orthodox commentary; the repository's records describe a patristics shelf of cards on the box (docs/archive/CONSOLIDATION.md:81-83), but nothing on the commentary shelf is patristic. The source is Thomas Aquinas's Catena Aurea, the Fathers and later writers gathered verse by verse on the four Gospels, in the English edition of 1841-45. Plan two answers checker-100's eight findings at line 4: CCEL holds only Matthew and Mark and asks permission to republish; the edition keys verses by leading text with typos and ranges, many paragraphs continue the one before, editors' notes sit inside the Fathers' words, and the edition has no list of writers; so a measure step chooses the source and commits a golden checked against the source before any parser is trusted, and the build runs through the gated path of run 2026-11-11-box-build. Plan three answers line 7: the words served are the 1841-45 printing's, read from its public-domain scans on archive.org and confirmed by a second independent reading, never a modern editor's; a transcription's permission follows the transcription it copies, so CCEL's text and any copy of it are used only to compare, never served; a Gospel with no second reading of the printing is left for a later run. Plan four answers line 10: the second reading of each Gospel is a second physical copy of the same printing, scanned and read separately on archive.org, named by item id; page furniture is removed by the OCR's own layout before any comparison; margin citations are read from the margin as citations, never as words; and an author or citation is served only where both copies' readings agree. Plan five answers line 13: an excerpt starts only at an author heading the printing marks (a known name set in small capitals and followed by a semicolon, as the layout file flags it) in both copies; the build parses streaming, under a memory cap, and records its peak; second readings are named per volume part. It also moves onto run 2026-11-11-box-build's design: the build adds data/builds/catena-aurea/<hash>/, and the shelf serves it only once a gated deploy ships the pin. Plan six answers line 16: the build's inputs (the author table, the golden, the item ids and the pinned hashes of what it fetches) travel with the tool as its listed inputs, as run 2026-11-11-box-build's plan six provides; and the first ship is graded by a check that the pinned build is on the box, chained before the deploy, and by the new probes read after it with a named revert, since the live assay refuses only a probe that has passed before. Plan seven answers line 19: the live check names its requests and its expected reading. Plan eight takes what step measure measured: an author heading ends with ';' after a full name and '.' after an abbreviated one; two copies of one typesetting agree on the same structural errors (a lost line-end hyphen, a margin word fused into the text, the ae ligature), so agreement is confirmed only after holds that target those errors; CCEL's transcription is not a third reading, since its own errors would hold about half the correct excerpts (checker-100, line 28); the golden's method and normalization are stated; and an author's language is filled only where the encyclopedia states it. Plan nine answers line 33: a heading is ';' or '.' after any name or abbreviation the table holds (full names end in '.' too, as ALCUIN., JEROME. and nearly every head in John), and two more holds catch the shared errors step measure found: a token outside letters and the stated punctuation, or on the census's list of misreadings (such as 'fyc.' for '&c.'), and a word flagged as a superscript that is not a footnote mark answered on its page. Plan ten answers builder-30's note at line 49: step catena reopens as catena2 with the canary listing test, the golden and the author table in scope; two golden verses are corrected from the page; a verse both copies misread alike is held by its order in the chapter, and a confirmed verse that differs from the golden refuses the build; Mark's CHRYS. carries the editors' mark; the italic-I hold no longer depends on a list of verbs; the Matthew 1:1 test names what the build serves and holds there, and the Gloss is tested at Matthew 1:17; the MCP tool's description names the Catena.

findings: CATENA (plan ten, line 51), the italic-I hold: 'an italic run whose first word is lower case where a sentence or the excerpt begins' misses the golden's own cases. In this printing a dropped italic I opens a quotation in mid-sentence, after a comma. Matthew-t01-p866 (italic_capital_i_misread): 'It follows, I was an hungred', OCR '/'. John-s09-p418: 'how we shall understand this, I will not judge', OCR 'this, / will'. If both copies drop the I, the italic run opens 'was' or 'will' after a comma, not where a sentence begins. The plan's hold passes it, and the Father's sentence is served with its first word gone. The saved build's rule (tools/build_catena.py:617) holds the first word of any italic run, wherever it opens, when that word is a listed verb; plan ten drops the list but also narrows the place. To answer: hold any italic run whose first word is lower case, wherever it opens (unless the golden settles it). Quotations in this printing open with a capital, so the cost is yield: italic Latin words such as 'curialis' (Mark-s12-p330's page) are held too. And name the two golden cases above as its tests.

CATENA and TESTS (plan ten, line 51), the verse guard: 'a golden excerpt whose verse both copies confirm and which differs from the golden refuses the build' contradicts 'a section whose verse both copies misread alike is held (Matthew-s10-p32)'. Both copies read Matthew-s10-p32 alike, as 1:2, and the golden reads 1:12-15. If 'confirm' means 'read alike', every build refuses. 'Confirm' must mean that the verse passed every verse hold. The order hold is also not enough on its own, and it is underspecified. (a) The saved build's check that the running heads allow the range (tools/build_catena.py rhead_allows; 'verse not in the running head' was the first hold on 6 golden excerpts) is not in the plan, though it is the independent printed check. (b) 'In order between the sections before and after it' says nothing of the printing's own overlaps (Matthew 1 prints '3-6.' then '6-8.') or of the Vulgate order (Matthew 5 prints verse 5 before verse 4). If overlaps are allowed, a range end that both copies misread one verse long into the next section's first verse stays in order and inside the page's running head, so a section's comments are served on the next verse too: another verse's words. To answer: a section's verse is served only when both copies read it alike, the running heads allow it, its own verse marks run on without a gap, and it follows its neighbours with no overlap beyond the single verse the printing shares. 'Confirm' means all four. A section that fails any of them is held, and the Vulgate-ordered sections are held or listed from the census.

text: checker-100 on plan eleven (line 53), 2026-11-12. These measurements were read in the main checkout and in archive.org page images; nothing was written. (1) The printing numbers verses by the English Bible, but groups the comments as the Vulgate divides the text. Copy A of Mark, catenaaureacomme02thomuoft: page 163 (n174) has the running head 'VER. 34—38. ST. MARK.', and in that section Theophylact, Bede and Pseudo-Chrysostom comment on 'Verily I say unto you, That there be some of them that stand here who shall not taste of death'. The next page (n175) opens 'CHAP. IX. 1. And he said unto them, Verily I say unto you, That there be some of them that stand here, which shall not taste of death', the English 9:1, printed as a lemma before '2. And after six days'. So the Fathers' words on the English 9:1 stand in the section headed 8:34-38, as the Vulgate's 8:39. Matthew 5 agrees: it prints the meek as '5.' though it sets them before '4.'. (2) data/bible_en.jsonl is the World English Bible. Among the 89 Gospel chapters it differs from data/bible_la.jsonl in verse count or verse numbers in exactly the lead's seven. In Luke 17 the English has verses 1-35 and 37, with no verse 36, so its count, 36, is not its last verse, 37. The English holds Matthew 17:21, 18:11, 23:14, Mark 7:16, 9:44, 9:46, 11:26, 15:28, Luke 23:17 and John 5:4. (3) Per-verse Latin-to-English word ratios, in the 82 chapters outside the seven (3,458 verses, median 0.739), point to verses the Vulgate divides otherwise in chapters whose counts are equal. Read in both texts: at Luke 4:18/19 the Latin 19 opens at 'prædicare captivis', the English 18's second half. At Luke 9:42/43 the Latin 43 opens at 'Et increpavit Jesus', the English 42b. At John 4:13/14 the Latin 13 runs into the English 14a. At John 10:41/42 the Latin 42 opens at 'Omnia autem quæcumque dixit Joannes', the English 41b. At Matthew 16:2/3 the Latin 3 is only 'Et mane: Hodie tempestas'. Matthew 27:35 differs in text: the Latin keeps the psalm, and the English drops it.

findings: CATENA NUMBERING and BASE (plan eleven, line 53): equal verse counts are not enough, and the plan names the wrong mechanism. (a) The printing numbers by the English Bible. Copy A of Mark, n175, opens 'CHAP. IX. 1. And he said unto them, Verily I say unto you ... shall not taste of death'. Aquinas groups the comments as the Vulgate divides the text: on page 163 (n174, running head 'VER. 34—38.') Theophylact, Bede and Pseudo-Chrysostom comment on those 9:1 words inside the section 8:34-38. The hazard is a section boundary that falls where the Vulgate divides the text differently from the English, whatever the chapter's count. (b) Such boundaries exist inside chapters whose counts are equal: Luke 4:18/19 (the Latin 19 opens at 'prædicare captivis', the English 18b), Luke 9:42/43 (the Latin 43 opens at 'Et increpavit Jesus', the English 42b), John 4:13/14, John 10:41/42 (the Latin 42 opens at the English 41b) and Matthew 16:2/3, all read in data/bible_la.jsonl and data/bible_en.jsonl. tools/catena_aurea/gospel_verses.json, derived by counts, would treat these chapters as divided alike. Where Aquinas breaks a section at the Latin boundary, a Father's words on one English verse are served on the next. (c) Luke 17 counts 36 in the engine's English because verse 36 is missing from it (World English Bible), and its last verse is 37. A file of counts gives condition (3) the wrong last verse. Holding the seven chapters whole is a sound line for this run, and reading the printing's numbering adds nothing, since the printing is already in English numbers. To answer: derive the divisions by verse, not by count. List each pair of adjacent verses the Latin divides differently (found by code, read in both texts by the builder, re-derived and read by the step's checker), and store each chapter's verse numbers as present. Hold every section whose first or last verse sits at such a pair, as well as the seven chapters. Have the step's note read one such place in the printing (John 10:41-42) to show whether its sections break there.

An excerpt starts only at an author heading: a name or abbreviation the author table holds, set in small capitals as the layout file flags it, followed by ';' or '.', after a full name or an abbreviation alike, wherever on the line it falls; both copies must show the heading at the same place, or the excerpt is held. A name not flagged as small capitals, or followed by neither ';' nor '.', is words, never a heading. Before any comparison, five holds target the errors two copies of one typesetting share: an excerpt is held where a line's last word and the next line's first word together form a word found elsewhere in that volume (a lost hyphen), where any word's box crosses the text column's edge (a margin word fused into the text), where the ligature ae or a word read as 'ae' occurs, where a token holds a character outside letters and the stated punctuation (. , ; : ? ! ' " ( ) - and the dash, with '&' only in '&c.') or is on the census's list of misreadings (such as 'fyc.' for '&c.'), and where a word is flagged as a superscript but is not a footnote mark answered by a footnote on that page (as 'that' in John 1:3), in each case unless the page image check in the golden has settled that word. An excerpt is served only when its words, as read from the two copies after these steps and the stated normalization (whitespace, declared encoding), are equal; its author is served only when both copies give the same name after folding small capitals and case, else the excerpt is held; its citation is served only when both copies' margin readings agree after the same folding, else it is served as 'citation not confirmed' and counted. Every held excerpt and unconfirmed citation is counted per Gospel in the step's note against the measure step's expectation, and every golden excerpt the build serves equals the golden, words, author and citation. A range is stored as a range, with a field this source adds and the other sources never read. A paragraph continues the excerpt above only where the printing's structure shows it; a paragraph the parser cannot attribute with certainty is not served and is counted. Editors' notes are never served as a Father's words. Parsing never touches the network beyond the named fetches and never resolves an external entity or document type definition. The tool exits non-zero on any golden mismatch or changed source, so no build directory is added. The tool imports only the standard library and is deterministic; the step adds its entry to tools/box_builds.txt with the output's sha256, a memory cap, and its inputs: the author table, the golden, the item ids and chapters per volume part, and the pinned hashes of every file it fetches, which reach the box with the tool; the tool reads no other repository file, and the listed hash comes from a run with exactly these inputs; and src/concordance/build_pins.json gains the same hash. The tool writes its output as bytes with '\n' line ends on every platform, so the hash computed on Windows is the hash the box computes. Both copies of one typesetting can misread a verse mark alike (Matthew-s10-p32 reads 1:2 in both, where the page prints 1:12-15), so a section's verse or range is confirmed only when all of these hold, and only a confirmed section is served: (1) both copies read it alike; (2) the page's running heads allow it; (3) it begins at the verse after the end of the section before it in its chapter, as both copies read that section, with no verse skipped, a chapter's first section beginning at verse 1 and its last ending at the chapter's last verse in the engine's numbering; (4) it overlaps no neighbour. The printing's own overlaps (Matthew 1 prints '3-6.' then '6-8.') and its sections set in the Vulgate's order (Matthew 5 prints verse 5 before verse 4) fail and are held, a cost in yield, since a range end misread one verse long reads exactly as a shared verse does. A golden excerpt whose section is confirmed and whose verse differs from the golden refuses the build, as a mismatch in words, author or citation does. NUMBERING: the printing numbers verses as the English Bible does, but Aquinas groups the comments as the Vulgate divides the text: on Mark's page 163, headed 'VER. 34—38.', Theophylact, Bede and Pseudo-Chrysostom comment on the words of the English Mark 9:1, the Vulgate's 8:39 (checker-100, line 54). The engine's own Clementine Vulgate and English texts (data/bible_la.jsonl, data/bible_en.jsonl) differ in verse count or numbers in seven Gospel chapters, Matthew 17, Mark 4, 8 and 9, Luke 17, John 6 and John 11, which are held whole, counted, and named for a later run with a versification map; inside the other chapters they divide some adjacent verses otherwise (checker-100 read Luke 4:18/19, Luke 9:42/43, John 4:13/14, John 10:41/42 and Matthew 16:2/3). Condition (3) reads a chapter's verses as the input lists them, never as a count. The step's note reads one such place in the printing, John 10:41-42, to show whether its sections break there. The italic-I hold reads the case as printed and holds any italic run whose first word is lower case, wherever it opens, unless the golden settles that word, since in this printing a dropped italic I opens a quotation in mid-sentence, after a comma (checker-100, line 52); the cost is yield, as italic Latin words are held too. """Derive tools/catena_aurea/gospel_verses.json from the engine's English and Latin texts (run 2026-11-11-fathers-shelf,

   that pair's English or Latin text (folding ae/oe ligatures and case), so a reading cites what is there.
"""

    return h.hexdigest()

    pairs = sorted(readings['pairs'], key=lambda p: (G.index(p['gospel']), p['chapter'], p['verses']))
    for p in pairs:
        k, (a, b) = (p['gospel'], p['chapter']), p['verses']
        assert b == a + 1 and a in en[k] and b in en[k] and k not in held, p
        here = fold(' '.join([en[k][a], en[k][b], la[k][a], la[k][b]]))

        assert any(G.index(p['gospel']) == r[1] and p['chapter'] == r[2] and r[3] in (a, b) for r in cands), p
    at = {(p['gospel'], p['chapter'], v): p for p in pairs for v in p['verses']}

        verdict = ('divided otherwise at ' + ', '.join('%d/%d' % tuple(p['verses']) for p in ps)) if ps else \
                  ('alike (text differs)' if ref in differs else 'alike')
        read.append({'verse': ref, 'ratio': round(r, 3), 'outside_band': not (lo <= r <= hi), 'read': verdict})
    out = {

3. Candidates, in every other chapter, by three detectors:

   (b) boundary punctuation: each boundary v/v+1 where one text's verse v ends a sentence ('.', '?' or '!') and the
       other's ends on a colon, or where the Latin verse ends on a verb of saying and a colon and the English ends a
       sentence, or the English ends on a verb of saying and ',' or ':' and the Latin ends a sentence (a speech
       formula carried across);
   (c) speech-formula position: each boundary where a verb of saying opens one text's verse v+1 and closes the other
       text's verse v, and not the other way round in either (a speech formula, or the one word 'saying', moved).
   Every candidate must have been read: it is listed with its verdict, and every listed pair must touch a candidate.

import hashlib
import json
import re
import sys

G = ('Matthew', 'Mark', 'Luke', 'John')
CLOSE = '"\'”’»)]'
SAY_LA = re.compile(r'\b(dix\w*|dic\w*|ait|aiunt|ajebat\w*|inquit|respond\w*|interrog\w*|clam\w*|loquens|locutus\w*|'
                    r'vocifer\w*|exclam\w*|mandav\w*|praecep\w*|praecep\w*|testat\w*|confess\w*|orabat|oravit|rogav\w*|'
                    r'rogabat\w*|increpav\w*|comminat\w*|docebat|scrib\w*)\b', re.I)
SAY_EN = re.compile(r'\b(said|saying|says|say|answered|asked|cried|spoke|told|tells|exclaimed|commanded|warned|replied)\b',
                    re.I)


def sha(p):
    h = hashlib.sha256()
    with open(p, 'rb') as fh:
        for b in iter(lambda: fh.read(1 << 20), b''):
            h.update(b)
    return h.hexdigest()

    d = {}

        for line in fh:
            o = json.loads(line)
            if o['book'] in G:
                d.setdefault((o['book'], o['chapter']), {})[o['verse']] = o['text']
    return d

    s = s.replace('æ', 'ae').replace('Æ', 'Ae').replace('œ', 'oe').replace('Œ', 'Oe')
    return re.sub(r'\s+', ' ', s).lower()


def end(t):
    t = t.rstrip().rstrip(CLOSE).rstrip()
    return t[-1:] if t else ''


def punctuation(e1, l1):
    """Detector (b) at the boundary after verse v (e1, l1: verse v in English and Latin)."""
    ee, le = end(e1), end(l1)
    tail_l, tail_e = ' '.join(l1.split()[-4:]), ' '.join(e1.split()[-4:])
    return bool((le == ':' and ee in ('.', '?', '!')) or (ee == ':' and le in ('.', '?', '!'))
                or (le == ':' and SAY_LA.search(tail_l) and ee in ('.', '?', '!'))
                or (ee in (':', ',') and SAY_EN.search(tail_e) and le in ('.', '?', '!')))


def speech_position(e1, e2, l1, l2):
    """Detector (c) at the boundary between verses v and v+1."""
    e1, e2, l1, l2 = e1.split(), e2.split(), l1.split(), l2.split()

    def has(rx, words):
        return bool(rx.search(' '.join(words)))
    fwd = has(SAY_EN, e2[:5]) and not has(SAY_LA, l2[:5]) and has(SAY_LA, l1[-6:]) and not has(SAY_EN, e1[-6:])
    rev = has(SAY_LA, l2[:5]) and not has(SAY_EN, e2[:5]) and has(SAY_EN, e1[-6:]) and not has(SAY_LA, l1[-6:])
    return fwd or rev


def main(argv):
    en_p, la_p, rd_p, out_p = argv[:4]

    readings = json.load(open(rd_p, encoding='utf-8'))
    keys = sorted(en, key=lambda k: (G.index(k[0]), k[1]))
    assert sorted(en) == sorted(la) and len(keys) == 89
    held = [k for k in keys if sorted(en[k]) != sorted(la[k])]
    ratios, bounds = [], []
    for k in keys:
        if k in held:
            continue
        vs = sorted(en[k])
        for v in vs:
            ratios.append((len(la[k][v].split()) / len(en[k][v].split()), G.index(k[0]), k[1], v))
        for v, w in zip(vs, vs[1:]):
            found = [n for n, hit in (('boundary punctuation', punctuation(en[k][v], la[k][v])),
                                      ('speech-formula position', speech_position(en[k][v], en[k][w], la[k][v],
                                                                                  la[k][w]))) if hit]
            if found:
                bounds.append((G.index(k[0]), k[1], v, w, found))
    ratios.sort()
    median = ratios[len(ratios) // 2][0]
    outside = [r for r in ratios if r[0] < lo or r[0] > hi]
    inside = [r for r in ratios if lo <= r[0] <= hi]
    nearest = inside[:near] + inside[-near:]
    cands = sorted(outside + nearest, key=lambda r: r[1:])
    pairs = sorted(readings['pairs'], key=lambda p: (G.index(p['gospel']), p['chapter'], p['verses']))
    for p in pairs:
        k, (a, b) = (p['gospel'], p['chapter']), p['verses']
        assert b == a + 1 and a in en[k] and b in en[k] and k not in held, p
        here = fold(' '.join([en[k][a], en[k][b], la[k][a], la[k][b]]))
        for q in re.findall(r"(?:^|[\s(])'([^']+)'(?=[\s,.;:)]|$)", p['reading']):
            assert fold(q) in here, (p, q)
        gi = G.index(p['gospel'])
        assert any(gi == r[1] and p['chapter'] == r[2] and r[3] in (a, b) for r in cands) or \
            any(gi == x[0] and p['chapter'] == x[1] and x[2] == a for x in bounds), p
    differs = set(readings['text_differs'])
    read = []

MEASURE changes nothing served. It surveys the 1841-45 printing's scans on archive.org (each volume and part, its item id and its rights mark quoted), the scans' own OCR text, and the transcriptions: CCEL's catena1 and catena2, and isidore.co's four pages, whose Matthew and Mark copy CCEL's transcription and whose Luke and John are modernized (checker-100, line 6). For each it records which Gospels it holds, its rights statement, its count of replacement characters, its counts of the printing's old forms (such as shews, hath, saith, thee, thou) against the scan's, and the structure census: verse marks and their variants and typos, ranges, continuation paragraphs, quoted Gospel text such as 'It goes on:', margin notes that change the attribution, and editors' notes. The words served are the printing's. A transcription that differs from the scan beyond listed transcription typos is never served; a transcription's permission follows the transcription it copies, not the site that hosts it, so CCEL's transcription and isidore.co's copy of it are compared against, never served, unless CCEL grants permission. The step names, for each volume part of each Gospel, two archive.org items that are scans of different physical copies of the 1841-45 printing, each with its own OCR, by item id and the chapters each holds (checker-100 found that catenaaureacomme03thomuoft holds Luke I-X while catenaaureacomme03thom holds I-XXIV, so Luke XI-XXIV needs a third item, probably p2catenaaureacom03thomuoft), and the share of excerpts it expects to serve; no OCR is run by this run. A chapter without two such copies is named for a later run and not served here. It also records which layout file each item offers (such as the OCR's page XML with word coordinates), since the rules below read it.

THE GOLDEN, committed at step measure: at least 30 excerpts for every Gospel this run serves, chosen by a fixed seed and including the hard cases the census found (a range, a continuation, an inline editor's note, a margin note, a quoted 'It goes on:'). Each holds the printing's words as read from the scan's page image: copied by code from one copy's OCR and checked word by word against that page image by eye, every correction listed and applied by code, normalized only by folding curly quotes and removing a space before punctuation, with the archive.org item and page, its verse or range, its author as printed, its citation, and its editors' notes kept apart. The step's checker checks each against the page image. The golden is the test of the parser and of the confirming reading; neither makes it. Among the hard cases: an excerpt that runs across a page break, an excerpt beside a margin citation, a page with a footnote, a running head inside an excerpt's span, a word with a real hyphen at a line end (such as 'money-changer'), and an author's name in small capitals. Also: an excerpt that begins mid-line, and an author's name standing inside another Father's words, which must stay his words and never start an excerpt. Step catena2 corrects two verse fields, each read again from the page image and listed as a correction applied by code: John-s20-p216 is John 6:1-14 and Luke-s11-p292 is Luke 8:40-48 (builder-30, line 49: both copies' ranges and running heads give them so).

AUTHORS: a committed table holds every attribution the census finds, each with dates read from its article in the Catholic Encyclopedia (1907-14, public domain) as the golden is read, from the page image with corrections listed, stored as printed or left out with the reason, and with Greek or Latin only where the article states it, else 'not stated'; writers after the age of the Fathers, such as the Gloss, Remigius and Rabanus, are labelled later writers; 'Pseudo-' authors stay distinct; an ascription the editors dispute is kept with their mark. An attribution the table does not hold is served as printed and never guessed. The shelf names itself the Fathers and later writers that Aquinas gathered, in the English edition of 1841-45, crediting the translators as the edition's own prefaces name them, never a catalogue's metadata. In Mark, the head CHRYS. is served as printed with the editors' mark the author table already quotes from Mark's preface, which gives most of those passages to Victor of Antioch; there it is never named John Chrysostom without that mark.

CATENA: the build fetches, for each volume part served, both copies' OCR layout files with word coordinates and the small-capitals flag, parses them streaming, never whole, and runs under its listed memory cap with the full build's peak recorded in the step's note; and from each copy, before any comparison, removes the page furniture by its place on the page as the coordinates give it: the running head and page number at the top, footnotes below the text, and the margin column, whose text is kept apart as the citations of the excerpts it stands beside and is never part of a Father's words. Line-end hyphens are read by one stated rule: a hyphen is kept where the hyphenated form occurs elsewhere in that volume's text and the joined form does not, joined where the joined form occurs and the hyphenated does not, and otherwise the excerpt is held. An excerpt starts only at an author heading: a name or abbreviation the author table holds, set in small capitals as the layout file flags it, followed by ';' or '.', after a full name or an abbreviation alike, wherever on the line it falls; both copies must show the heading at the same place, or the excerpt is held. A name not flagged as small capitals, or followed by neither ';' nor '.', is words, never a heading. Before any comparison, five holds target the errors two copies of one typesetting share: an excerpt is held where a line's last word and the next line's first word together form a word found elsewhere in that volume (a lost hyphen), where any word's box crosses the text column's edge (a margin word fused into the text), where the ligature ae or a word read as 'ae' occurs, where a token holds a character outside letters and the stated punctuation (. , ; : ? ! ' " ( ) - and the dash, with '&' only in '&c.') or is on the census's list of misreadings (such as 'fyc.' for '&c.'), and where a word is flagged as a superscript but is not a footnote mark answered by a footnote on that page (as 'that' in John 1:3), in each case unless the page image check in the golden has settled that word. An excerpt is served only when its words, as read from the two copies after these steps and the stated normalization (whitespace, declared encoding), are equal; its author is served only when both copies give the same name after folding small capitals and case, else the excerpt is held; its citation is served only when both copies' margin readings agree after the same folding, else it is served as 'citation not confirmed' and counted. Every held excerpt and unconfirmed citation is counted per Gospel in the step's note against the measure step's expectation, and every golden excerpt the build serves equals the golden, words, author and citation. A range is stored as a range, with a field this source adds and the other sources never read. A paragraph continues the excerpt above only where the printing's structure shows it; a paragraph the parser cannot attribute with certainty is not served and is counted. Editors' notes are never served as a Father's words. Parsing never touches the network beyond the named fetches and never resolves an external entity or document type definition. The tool exits non-zero on any golden mismatch or changed source, so no build directory is added. The tool imports only the standard library and is deterministic; the step adds its entry to tools/box_builds.txt with the output's sha256, a memory cap, and its inputs: the author table, the golden, the item ids and chapters per volume part, and the pinned hashes of every file it fetches, which reach the box with the tool; the tool reads no other repository file, and the listed hash comes from a run with exactly these inputs; and src/concordance/build_pins.json gains the same hash. The tool writes its output as bytes with '\n' line ends on every platform, so the hash computed on Windows is the hash the box computes. Both copies of one typesetting can misread a verse mark alike (Matthew-s10-p32 reads 1:2 in both, where the page prints 1:12-15), so a section's verse or range is confirmed only when all of these hold, and only a confirmed section is served: (1) both copies read it alike; (2) the page's running heads allow it; (3) it begins at the verse after the end of the section before it in its chapter, as both copies read that section, with no verse skipped, a chapter's first section beginning at verse 1 and its last ending at the chapter's last verse in the engine's numbering; (4) it overlaps no neighbour. The printing's own overlaps (Matthew 1 prints '3-6.' then '6-8.') and its sections set in the Vulgate's order (Matthew 5 prints verse 5 before verse 4) fail and are held, a cost in yield, since a range end misread one verse long reads exactly as a shared verse does. A golden excerpt whose section is confirmed and whose verse differs from the golden refuses the build, as a mismatch in words, author or citation does. NUMBERING: the printing numbers verses as the English Bible does, but Aquinas groups the comments as the Vulgate divides the text: on Mark's page 163, headed 'VER. 34—38.', Theophylact, Bede and Pseudo-Chrysostom comment on the words of the English Mark 9:1, the Vulgate's 8:39 (checker-100, line 54). So a section boundary where the Vulgate divides the text otherwise than the engine's English would serve a Father's words on one English verse under the next. The engine's own Clementine Vulgate and English texts (data/bible_la.jsonl, data/bible_en.jsonl) differ in verse count or numbers in seven Gospel chapters, Matthew 17, Mark 4, 8 and 9, Luke 17, John 6 and John 11, which are held whole, counted, and named for a later run with a versification map; inside the other chapters they divide some adjacent verses otherwise (checker-100 read Luke 4:18/19, Luke 9:42/43, John 4:13/14, John 10:41/42 and Matthew 16:2/3). Every such pair is listed: candidates are found by code, as each verse whose Latin-to-English word ratio lies outside a band the note states, and every candidate is read in both texts by the builder, then re-derived and read by the step's checker; a section whose first or last verse sits at a listed pair is held. Condition (3) reads a chapter's verses as the input lists them, never as a count. The step's note reads one such place in the printing, John 10:41-42, to show whether its sections break there. The italic-I hold reads the case as printed and holds any italic run whose first word is lower case, wherever it opens, unless the golden settles that word, since in this printing a dropped italic I opens a quotation in mid-sentence, after a comma (checker-100, line 52); the cost is yield, as italic Latin words are held too. Each golden excerpt the build matches to no head is named in the step's note with the reason.
